title: Writing Task 1: Process
topic: Menjelaskan diagram proses dengan urutan tahap yang jelas
objectives: Mengenali tahap dan urutan dalam diagram proses
Memakai kata penghubung urutan dengan tepat
Menjelaskan perubahan bahan dari satu bentuk ke bentuk lain

youtube.videoDescription: Video 10 sampai 15 menit tentang cara menjelaskan diagram proses dari awal sampai akhir, dengan kata penghubung urutan dan bentuk pasif.

lesson.intro: Diagram proses menunjukkan bagaimana sesuatu dibuat atau diubah melalui beberapa tahap. Kunci menulisnya adalah urutan yang jelas dan bentuk pasif untuk menyebut tindakan tanpa menyebut pelaku.

sections.heading: Tahap dan fase
sections.bodyMd: Setiap **stage** diberi kata urutan. **Phase** dipakai untuk bagian yang lebih besar. Jika proses dimulai lagi, sebut itu sebagai **cycle**.

sections.heading: Prosedur dan perubahan
sections.bodyMd: **Procedure** menjelaskan cara melakukan tahap. Gunakan **transform** atau **convert** untuk perubahan bentuk bahan, dan **generate** untuk sesuatu yang dihasilkan.

sections.heading: Urutan
sections.bodyMd: Pakai **subsequently** untuk langkah berikutnya dan **finally** untuk tahap terakhir. Jangan menaruh tahap terakhir di awal kalimat.

block3.title: Proses Daur Ulang Kertas
block3.text:
The diagram describes the process of turning waste paper into new paper. The process has four main stages, and each stage is part of a longer cycle. Understanding each phase helps readers see how the final product is made, and why each step matters.

In the first stage, used paper is collected from offices, schools, and households. Workers sort the paper by type and remove plastic covers, staples, and tape. This procedure is important because contaminated paper is difficult to transform into a useful product.

In the second stage, the sorted paper is mixed with water and broken down into pulp. The pulp is a thick liquid that contains small fibres. Machines then clean the pulp and remove ink, which is the main challenge for recycling. Some plants use a special chemical to help convert the ink into a form that can be filtered out.

The third phase is the forming stage. The clean pulp is spread across a wide mesh belt, where water drains away and a thin sheet begins to form. The sheet is pressed between rollers, and this step helps generate a smooth surface. Heat is then applied to dry the paper completely. This drying phase is closely monitored, because uneven moisture can weaken the final sheet and cause tearing during printing.

Subsequently, the dry paper is cut into rolls or sheets and checked for quality. Samples are tested for strength and brightness, and any defective batch is returned to the start of the cycle. This loop allows the factory to reuse material again and again, which reduces waste and saves water.

Finally, the finished paper is packed and sent to printers, shops, and publishers. The whole process can take several days, depending on the machines and the weather. Many factories now record data at each stage, so they can improve the procedure over time and report their results clearly. Readers who compare this diagram with a similar process for glass or metal will notice that the stages are broadly alike. The main difference lies in the second stage, where chemicals are used to remove colour or other contaminants. Overall, the diagram shows a clear and repeatable process that any trained operator can follow from the first step to the last.
